Building Construction Illustrated from 1975 isn't exactly a classic. My dad was given it when he was an apprentice carpenter by his mentor/employer. When I took up the business he dug it out, but it was water damaged and rat gnawed on the edges. I cut some cardboard and used the biggest panels I could cut from a leather coat. It took me a night to stitch it together. Now when I tell people I'm going by the book I can pull out "the book." A few things have changed, but the illustrations are great for explaining things to customers. (No more napkin doodles.) The internet is great for info and all, but I'm a sucker for tradition. I can't wait to go grey, so that I can look like a wizard every time I blow the dust off this puppy.

Yup. Awl with a regular pattern. I use 2 needles and a sort of figure 8 pattern, with this hand me down "friendship bracelet" cord my sister amassed an inexhaustible supply of 15 years ago.
